description:
### Figure Description

This is a single-panel, landscape-oriented diagram illustrating the training pipeline for a sparse Large Language Model (LLM) using knowledge distillation from a dense LLM. The overall aesthetic is clean, professional, and publication-ready, embodying the "Soft Tech & Scientific Pastels" style suitable for a top-tier academic venue.

**1. Overall Layout:**
The diagram follows a horizontal, left-to-right flow, structured in a gentle Y-shape. An input element on the far left splits into two parallel processing tracks that run horizontally. The upper track represents the frozen, dense teacher model, while the lower track represents the trainable, sparse student model. These two tracks converge on the far right into a single module representing the loss calculation. The entire composition is set against a pure white background with generous spacing between all elements to ensure clarity and focus.

**2. Components:**

*   **Input (Far Left):**
    *   A small, horizontally-oriented rectangle with softly rounded corners, labeled "**Input *x***".
    *   **Style:** It has a soft off-white fill and a delicate, medium gray border. The text is a bold, dark charcoal serif font. A very subtle drop shadow gives it a slight lift from the page.

*   **Upper Track - Dense Model (Center-Left):**
    *   A large rounded rectangle prominently labeled "**Dense LLM**" in a bold, dark navy serif font.
    *   Below the title, a subtitle in a smaller, muted gray sans-serif italic font reads "[frozen] · full forward pass", indicating the model's weights are static.
    *   **Style:** The box has a clean white fill, framed by a crisp, defining dark navy border. It includes a subtle drop shadow.

*   **Lower Track - Sparse Model (Center-Left, aligned below the Dense LLM):**
    *   A slightly taller rounded rectangle labeled "**Sparse LLM**" in a bold, slate blue serif font.
    *   It contains two lines of descriptive text. The first, in a dark serif font, reads: "Predictor *f*<sub>θ</sub> -> Gumbel-Sigmoid -> Mask". The second, in a smaller, muted gray sans-serif italic, provides implementation details: "<1% params | x32 layers".
    *   **Style:** The box has a pale, cool blue fill, suggesting its active, trainable state, and is enclosed by a confident slate blue border. It also features a subtle drop shadow.

*   **Output Distributions (Center-Right):**
    *   To the right of the "Dense LLM" box is a small, pill-shaped badge labeled "**p<sub>dense</sub>**". It has a solid dark navy fill with the text in bold white.
    *   To the right of the "Sparse LLM" box is a matching pill-shaped badge labeled "**p<sub>sparse</sub>**". It has a solid slate blue fill with the text in bold white.

*   **Loss Calculation (Far Right):**
    *   A large rounded rectangle, vertically centered between the two tracks, where the paths converge.
    *   It contains the primary mathematical formula "**D<sub>KL</sub>( p<sub>dense</sub> || p<sub>sparse</sub> )**" in a large, bold, dark charcoal serif font.
    *   A subtitle below the formula in muted gray sans-serif italic font clarifies the backpropagation path: "Gradients to θ only".
    *   **Style:** The box has a warm, inviting cream fill, highlighted by a prominent warm amber border that draws focus to the objective function. It is finished with a subtle drop shadow.

**3. Connections (Arrows):**
All arrows are elegant with small, sharp arrowheads, ensuring a professional look.

*   **Input Split:** Two slender, neutral gray arrows originate from the right edge of the "Input x" box.
    *   One arrow travels diagonally upwards to the left edge of the "Dense LLM" box.
    *   The other arrow travels diagonally downwards to the left edge of the "Sparse LLM" box.
*   **Forward Pass:**
    *   A short, horizontal gray arrow connects the "Dense LLM" box to the "p<sub>dense</sub>" pill.
    *   A short, horizontal gray arrow connects the "Sparse LLM" box to the "p<sub>sparse</sub>" pill.
*   **Loss Input:**
    *   A slightly bolder dark navy arrow, matching the dense model's color, extends from the "p<sub>dense</sub>" pill diagonally downwards to the "KL Loss" box.
    *   A corresponding slate blue arrow extends from the "p<sub>sparse</sub>" pill diagonally upwards to the "KL Loss" box, visually linking the sparse model to the loss.
*   **Backpropagation:**
    *   A fine, **dashed** gray arrow gracefully originates from the bottom of the "KL Loss" box, loops underneath the lower track, and points to the bottom of the "Sparse LLM" box, clearly indicating the gradient path.
    *   A small, gray italic label "**backprop**" is placed near the midpoint of this arrow.

**4. Labels and Annotations:**

*   **Bottom Annotation Bar:** A thin, gray dotted line spans the entire width of the figure at the bottom, separating the main diagram from a summary annotation bar.
    *   On the left side of this bar, the text reads: "**Training: soft masks via Gumbel-Sigmoid**" in a bold charcoal serif font.
    *   On the right side, the text reads: "**Inference: hard masks via TEAL global top-k**" in a matching bold charcoal serif font. This clearly contrasts the two operational modes.

**5. Styling Summary:**
*   **Color Palette:** A sophisticated and harmonious palette is used: dark navy for the static dense model, a lively slate blue for the trainable sparse model, and a contrasting warm amber for the loss function. Neutral grays and charcoals provide clarity for text and connections.
*   **Fonts:** A classic, professional serif font is used for all primary labels and titles, lending a formal, academic feel. A clean sans-serif font is used for secondary annotations and subtitles for maximum readability.
*   **Visual Effects:** All rectangular components feature soft, rounded corners and a consistent, subtle drop shadow that gives them a gentle lift from the background, enhancing the sense of depth and organization.
*   **Line Work:** Lines are thin and precise. The backpropagation arrow is distinctly styled as dashed to differentiate it from the solid lines representing the forward data flow.
